bevel.note: photo-measured - the housing is an octagon in section: the four edges that run from the port face to the back are cut off, which is what the user and the photographs call its wedge. The front's silhouette (front image, 4.407 px/mm) narrows 10.9 mm at its top and bottom rows and reaches full width 16.3 mm in, at every corner; the four product images give identical silhouettes, quantised to 1.8 mm by the image's mask, so 11 and 16 are good to about two millimetres. The video (0:31-0:41) shows these cuts running the whole depth. THE GREY BANDS BESIDE THE LEGEND PLATE ARE BEVELS TOO, which a first draft of this model read as flat casting and the maintainer corrected from the explorer: in the video's three-quarter frames (0:29-0:33, and the render at 0:46) the band right of the plate is lit as its own plane and its top edge slants up to meet the top face, and the back face (0:32) carries the same band between the plates and the fins. So the four edges between the front or back and the finned sides are bevelled as well, 12.6 mm across the face - the dark plate is 58.4 of the 83.8 mm, measured on the straight-on front - and taken at 45 degrees, because no view shows how far back along the side the bevel runs. The back is taken to match the front.

bottom-layout.note: estimated - the underside is not photographed. Drawn as plain casting, the bevels strips at its sides; registered as a gap.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Dimension (L*W*H) 5.71 x 4.33 x 3.30 in'. The letters are not width, height and depth: the straight-on front reads 0.587 wide-to-tall against 3.30/5.71 = 0.578, so L (145.0 mm) is the face's height as the unit hangs on the rail, H (83.8) its width and W (110.0) the depth from the port face to the DIN face.

front-layout.note: photo-measured on the straight-on AIS2003P front image at 4.407 px/mm (Gate 1: the face's own width agrees with the datasheet to 1.5 percent; the datasheet's front is the same artwork). Jack lamps located by colour; the eight-port block matches the AIS4001's (columns x 23.9 and 45.3, 15.57 mm pitch from y 43.2); the combo RJ45 halves 9-12 below it have lamps at x 24.2 and 45.5, y 108.1 and 123.4; the combo SFP halves are four cages in a column at x 49.9-59.9 from y 14.0 on a 14.5 mm pitch (the gold strip runs 13.8-71.5), with no lamps of their own. Jacks are drawn with the lamped ganged cell turned 90/270 so the keyways face out; its lamps are 8.3 mm apart against the jacks' 11.5, the closest library cell that fits the 11 mm column. The console is the bare ganged cell, turned the same way. Cages are std/sfp@1 on their side; each SFP lamp is a small dash drawn with common/led-rect-sm@1 turned 90.

lamps.note: photo-measured - each jack has two lamps, green at its top and amber at its bottom, and the faceplate's colour key pairs green with LINK/ACT and red-orange with PoE; so the green lamp is link/activity and the amber one PoE, set per placement because the two columns are turned opposite ways and swap led-a and led-b.

power.note: datasheet - 'Power Supply DC 48-57 V'; 'Idling: 48V 4.8W / 57V 5.13W'; 'Full load: 48V 195.36W / 57V 198.36W'; 'PoE Budget 185W'. power-max-w takes the highest figure (198.36 W); no ambient is stated with any of them. The supply is not included ('the power supply is excluded from the package').

rear-layout.note: estimated - the back render is foreshortened top to bottom; widths are taken as fractions of the face on the same image row, heights as fractions of 145 mm. Two wall plates (upper with its screws above the keyholes, lower with them below) and the DIN clip between them, centred. The DIN rail's centre line lies about 79 mm from the top of this face.

sfp-numbering.note: photo-measured - the combo ports are numbered on both halves: 9 and 10 over 11 and 12 on the RJ45 block (9 and 11 on the left), and 9-12 top to bottom on the SFP column's strip. The GbE rows read '1v ^2' and so on, odd ports on the left by the reading of the arrows.

side-layout.note: estimated - from the video (0:37-0:41, 0:55) and the three-quarter image: both sides are fins running front to back, with a recessed channel and a raised badge plate carrying the wordmark on the right side. The left side is not photographed square on and is drawn as fins only.

silkscreen.note: photo-measured - legends transcribed from the AIS2003P front image: Reset, SYS, PWR; Fast Ring and SCP with leaders to switches 1 and 2; CONSOLE; the port numbers as printed; LINK/ACT and PoE under their colour keys; the summary line '8 x GE | 4 x GE Base-T/SFP Combo | PoE+'. The AURCORE wordmark is printed as text: its A is drawn as a chevron mark, which is not reproduced (no logo marks).

sources.note: vendor datasheet (AIS2003P Data Sheet 1.0, 3 pages: spec table, and an annotated front and back figure that is the same artwork as the product images); the product page's three images (straight-on front, three-quarter front-top-right, and a back render raised to show the top face), 1000 px; and the vendor's AIS4000 Series video (YouTube MfK6WpjLsA8, 1080p), whose footage at 0:28-1:02 is a real AIS4001P, the same housing - the top, back and sides here are that unit's, with the AIS2003P's own power legend. No hardware guide or drawing is published (the Download Center holds the CLI, ACC and ACN manuals only).

top-layout.note: estimated - no straight-on top view exists. Positions are fractions of the top face in the back render (image 3, raised about 35 degrees), corrected with the parts' own sizes: the five-way power header (Phoenix MSTB-GF family, 35.56 mm) runs front to back with its pole legend '1 + - earth + - 2' on one side and POWER:48-57V DC on the other (read off this build's back render), pole 1 at the rear; the RELAY header and the ground screw with its earth symbol are near the front edge. The video (1:00-1:02) confirms every part and legend close up but not their places on the face. Good to a few millimetres.
